data.about: A semicircular masonry arch of 19 voussoirs stands on a support that can spread outward. The arch cracks into three hinges — at the crown extrados and at the haunch intrados on both sides — and its four rigid bodies rotate as the span grows. The thrust line through the three hinges is found with the three-point funicular method: one trial funicular per span gives a division point on the load line, and the parallels to the two span chords meet at the pole. While the thrust line stays inside the masonry the arch stands; when it exits beyond the moved support edge, the arch collapses.

steps.caption: step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: left: a semicircular arch ring (intrados and extrados) on the ground line; the dashed circles are its geometry. What happens when a support gives way?
steps.title: A masonry arch on its supports

steps.caption: left: radial joints on rays through the centre cut the ring into 19 equal voussoirs — the crown lies in the middle of the top stone
steps.title: Nineteen voussoirs

steps.caption: left: if the right support spreads outward (drag the white support handle!), the ring cracks open at three hinges: the crown extrados and the haunch intrados on either side (third joint) — four rigid bodies, and the crown drops
steps.title: Three hinges

steps.caption: left: every voussoir weighs 2 kN on the vertical through its centroid; the cracked crown stone counts as two halves — right: the 20 weights stacked tip-to-tail form the load line
steps.title: Weights and the load line

steps.caption: left: the thrust line must pass through the three hinges — the chords from the crown hinge to each haunch hinge (dashed) split the problem into two spans
steps.title: The two span chords

steps.caption: right: a trial pole o′₁ sends rays to the upper load line — left: from C on the crown vertical a trial funicular hangs across the left-span verticals to the hinge vertical; its closing string (dashed)
steps.title: Trial funicular, left span

steps.caption: right: through o′₁ parallel to the closing string to d₁ on the load line; through d₁ parallel to the left chord — the pole must lie on this line
steps.title: Division point d₁ → pole line 1

steps.caption: the same for the right span: trial pole o′₂, trial funicular from N, closing string, division point d₂ — through d₂ parallel to the right chord: both pole lines meet at THE pole o
steps.title: Right span → the pole o

steps.caption: left: the thrust line starts at the crown hinge, parallel to the crown ray — right: the ray from o to the crown division of the load line
steps.title: Through the crown hinge

steps.caption: left: side by side, each parallel to its ray of o, bending on every centroid vertical, down to the ground beside the left hinge — right: the rays of o to the upper load line
steps.title: Down the left half

steps.caption: left: the right half of the thrust line descends to the spread support — right: the rays of o to the lower load line
steps.title: Down the right half

steps.caption: right: the total weight W runs down the load line; reactions A and B close the triangle through o — left: the same thrusts push into the ground at the two exit points
steps.title: Reactions

steps.caption: drag the white support handle to the right: the hinges rotate, the crown sinks, o wanders and the thrust line flattens — the arch STANDS as long as its thrust line stays inside the masonry
steps.title: Spread the supports!

steps.caption: the construction lines retire; the thrust line is compression (blue). When the right exit passes outside the support edge, the thrust line leaves the masonry: YOUR ARCH JUST COLLAPSED (red). Drag back to save it
steps.title: Stable — or collapsed
